name: seven_sisters
title: Seven Sisters chalk cliffs, East Sussex, England
note: Vertical white chalk cliffs 50-160 m high, cut across a row of dry valleys (the "sisters"), from Cuckmere Haven east past Birling Gap toward Beachy Head.
grid: local azimuthal equidistant (sphere R=6371008.8 m) centred on centre_lat/centre_lon; x east, y north; row 0 = north edge; pixel centre x = (col + 0.5 - cols/2) * pixel_size_m, y = (rows/2 - row - 0.5) * pixel_size_m
data_note: Terrain Tiles carry the Environment Agency 2 m lidar on this coast, so the vertical chalk faces are resolved (one or two pixels wide at 6 m). A few straight survey-strip seams show as faint steps inland in the north-east corner.
sea_floor: every height at or below 0.3 m is set to -2 m: the sea surface is 0 m and the source's bathymetry is left out; 17 offshore patches of the source's sea data (each under 5% of the mainland) are sea as well

source.dataset: Terrain Tiles (Mapzen / Tilezen joerd), Terrarium PNG encoding, AWS Open Data elevation-tiles-prod
source.publisher: Mapzen / Linux Foundation Tilezen, hosted by AWS
source.native_resolution_m: 2 m on land (Environment Agency lidar, as Terrain Tiles carry it here)
source.licence: Open data, each underlying source credited: https://github.com/tilezen/joerd/blob/master/docs/attribution.md
source.attribution: Terrain Tiles (Tilezen joerd) from: EU-DEM, produced using Copernicus data and information funded by the European Union; SRTM and GMTED2010 courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey; ETOPO1, U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration; (where in the UK) (c) Environment Agency copyright and/or database right 2015; (where in the USA) 3DEP courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey
source.resampling: Gaussian low-pass (sigma 0.89 source px) then bilinear

licence: Open data, each underlying source credited: https://github.com/tilezen/joerd/blob/master/docs/attribution.md
attribution: Terrain Tiles (Tilezen joerd) from: EU-DEM, produced using Copernicus data and information funded by the European Union; SRTM and GMTED2010 courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey; ETOPO1, U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration; (where in the UK) (c) Environment Agency copyright and/or database right 2015; (where in the USA) 3DEP courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey
encoding: 16-bit greyscale PNG: height_m = height_min_m + v / 65535 * (height_max_m - height_min_m)
water_mask_encoding: 8-bit: 0 land, 255 sea, 128 + i the i-th lake of `water`
